headline: Core biz growth aided by ref-gas and fluoropolymers; battery chemical at cusp of scaling

highlights: Fluorochemicals growth was led by R-32, with initial capacity expected to reach full utilisation by Q3FY27, while R-134a production is on track for commissioning in Q4FY27.
Fluoropolymers continued to benefit from volume growth and improving realisations, with the company confident of sustaining 17–20% growth over the next couple of years.

Fluorochemicals revenue up 135% YoY to INR 6.1bn GFL’s revenue rose 45.5% YoY to INR 17.6bn, aided by 135% YoY/32.5% QoQ increase in fluorochemicals’ revenue to INR 6.1bn, driven by a ramp-up in R- 32.
The fluoropolymers segment’s revenue rose 21.9% YoY, supported by volume growth and a favourable product mix.
valuation: We retain our estimates for FY27/28E and TP of INR 5,380, valuing GFL at an unchanged FY29E P/E multiple of 35x.
Upside risk: 1) Upcycle in fluoropolymers with higher-than-expected pricing; and 2) better-than-expected offtake in battery materials.
The views and opinions expressed in this document may or may not match or may be contrary with the views, estimates, rating, and target price of the Retail Research.
watch: Capex outlook GFL reiterated its long-term battery materials investment commitment of INR 60bn, expected to be funded through INR 30–35bn of equity, INR 15bn of debt, and the balance through internal accruals.
Risks Downside risks: 1) Safety and environmental issues; and 2) execution in fluoropolymer and battery materials businesses.
